standard_prerequisites.name: The truncation limit identifications
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 2668-2678: U_i = lim over ([Delta]/[i])_{<= n}^opp for i <= n, and U_{n+1} = lim over ([Delta]/[n+1])_{<= n}^opp.

standard_prerequisites.name: The coskeleton construction template
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 2678-2686: the maps U-tilde(phi) are defined exactly as in this lemma, giving an (n+1)-truncated simplicial object with sk_n U-tilde = U.

standard_prerequisites.name: Representability of the compatibility relation
standard_prerequisites.use: U_{n+1} represents the functor of families (f_0, ..., f_{n+1}) in Mor(T, U_n) satisfying d^n_{j-1} f_i = d^n_i f_j for all i < j.

core_obligations: The extension (proof lines 2668-2686): using the limit identifications, define the structure maps of U-tilde for all phi : [i] -> [j] with i, j <= n+1 exactly as in the coskeleton-existence lemma; this yields an (n+1)-truncated simplicial object with sk_n U-tilde = U and U-tilde_{n+1} = U_{n+1}.

The adjunction, forward (lines 2688-2696): given gamma : sk_n V -> U, the morphisms f_i = gamma_n d^{n+1}_i : V_{n+1} -> U_n satisfy the displayed relations and hence define a unique morphism V_{n+1} -> U_{n+1} by representability.

The adjunction, converse (lines 2696-2698): given gamma' : V -> U-tilde, restrict to Delta_{<= n} to get an element of the right-hand side; the mutual-inverse verification is left to the reader (see notes).
proof_roadmap: Define the extension U-tilde via the limit descriptions of the truncated terms.
Build the adjunction map in the forward direction from the face relations.
Restrict back for the converse direction.
difficulty_reason: Extension lemma (statement 2644-2666, proof 2668-2698): the one-step coskeleton extension - the new term is a representable functor of compatible families, the structure maps are transplanted from the coskeleton-existence lemma, and the adjunction bijection is constructed in both directions; the only unverified step is the mutual-inverse check, recorded in the notes. H2: adjunction bookkeeping over established limit descriptions.
